messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed in region us-west for route /v1/generate (model: redwood-xl-1.3b). Error rate spike started ~2026-03-15T10:20Z. Paging on-call.

Alice M.: paging — I'm on. severity P1? customers reporting failed inference, some 504s from the gateway. will collect initial impact.

Ben S.: I see it in the scheduler dashboard — queue depth (batching queue) on us-west-scheduler-2 climbed from ~40 -> ~240 in <10m. HOL blocking: a few long-lived batches are preventing progress for short requests.

Chloe R.: logs from runtime show repeated KV cache misses + upstream timeouts to worker pods. gateway logs: `upstream read timeout` and `502 Bad Gateway` upstream errors.

Alice M.: immediate ask: can we (1) reduce batching window for this model/route, (2) route short/low-token requests to fallback model or smaller quantized variant, (3) scale up scheduler/worker pool? which is fastest?

Diego P.: fastest is toggling batching config per-route (disable or set max_batch_delay=0). I can flip a config in the control plane — that will force requests to go hot-path without waiting for batches. downside: token cost rises.

Ben S.: agree. also we should open a temporary routing rule to divert traffic to dedicated-capacity-west (if available) to drain pressure. Chloe, can we confirm model compatibility with dedicated pool?

Chloe R.: redwood-xl-1.3b is available in dedicated pool but the variant there uses 8-bit quant on a slightly older kernel — should be compatible. latency profile slightly higher per-token but avoids scheduler batching entirely.

Alice M.: plan: (A) flip route batching off for /v1/generate for redwood-xl-1.3b in us-west, (B) add fallback routing to dedicated pool for 10% of traffic, (C) scale scheduler replicas by +2. I will do A and C, Diego do B.

Eva K.: support note — notifying affected customers: some requests may see higher per-token cost/latency while we mitigate. asking for ETA update as soon as we have one.

Ben S.: runbook checks: batch-queue-saturation runbook recommends disabling batching for the model first. also check `scheduler.queue_evict` logs for head-of-line evictions.

Alice M.: executing: 
```
# toggle batching for route
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --region us-west --model redwood-xl-1.3b --set BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=0
# scale scheduler
kubectl scale deployment/us-west-scheduler --replicas=5 -n redwood
```

Chloe R.: watching pods. one worker in us-west-scheduler-2 has backlog stuck at ~18k KB/s of KV writes; restarting it might clear old stuck sessions. suggestion: cordon+drain that pod and let autoscaler recreate.

Diego P.: applying routing fallback now: adding temporary policy to send 10% traffic to dedicated-west.

Diego P.: `applied rollback-safe route: fallback=dEDICATED:us-west:10%` — monitoring.

Ben S.: metrics: after flip (BATCH_MAX_DELAY_MS=0) error rate dropped ~65% within 90s, p99 latency reduced from 6.8s -> 3.2s. batching queue depth decreased to ~60. still seeing intermittent 502s on older worker nodes.

Alice M.: proceeding to drain the node with stuck backlog (node: us-west-node-47). Chloe, please kick off drain.

Chloe R.: draining now: `kubectl drain us-west-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — pods are terminating. taking ~40s for in-flight requests to finish.

Frank L.: quick check: status page draft — "Investigating: increased 5xx and timeouts for inference in us-west. Mitigations in progress, partial routing to dedicated capacity. We'll update in 15 minutes." Should I publish?

Eva K.: publish now with note: mitigation steps include disabling batching for route and routing 10% to dedicated pool. tell customers to expect improved success rates.

Frank L.: published. linking in support tickets.

Ben S.: after drain, one problematic worker pod never came up due to OOM at startup logs — `OOMKilled during model load`. That explains some of the persistent 502s as requests got routed to restarting pods. increasing worker memory or reducing parallel loads recommended as postmortem.

Alice M.: for live mitigation, we should add an autoscaler override to limit concurrent model loads per node. Chloe, can you patch the runtime to reject new model loads if memory pressure > 85%?

Chloe R.: will open a quick emergency config: `MAX_CONCURRENT_LOADS=1` on us-west pool. Patching now.

Diego P.: routing heuristic update: switch to capacity-aware routing during incidents (prefer non-hot nodes). I've enabled capacity-aware policy for us-west to reduce routing to churn nodes.

Ben S.: current status: error rate stabilized near baseline (~10% above normal), p99 ~2.9s. gateway timeouts rare now. queue depth back to normal.

Alice M.: assigning follow-ups:
- Ben S.: investigate root cause of sudden queue spike (correlate with traffic pattern / client spike) — due EOD.
- Chloe R.: postmortem on OOM during model load and operator guard (MAX_CONCURRENT_LOADS) — assign infra-ml.
- Diego P.: add incident-safe routing toggle and test in staging — due in 3d.
- Eva K./Frank L.: customer communications and timeline — send follow-up email/notes.

Frank L.: ETA for full recovery?

Ben S.: will monitor for next 30m; if stable for 30m we'll mark mitigated and start post-incident.

Alice M.: marking mitigated -> partial: yes. keeping channel open for 30m monitoring. good work team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. responders: Alice M., Ben S., Chloe R., Diego P., Eva K., Frank L.

Alice M.: final note before handoff: add a regression alert on sudden queue depth > 3x baseline that alerts SRE + runtime team (not just paging on-call). Ben please include metric in follow-up.

Ben S.: will add alert rule `scheduler.queue_depth_ratio > 3` -> page SRE + runtime. created draft PR.

Chloe R.: I'll collect heap/oom traces from the affected node and push to the incident runbook artifacts.

Alice M.: thanks all. channel will be closed after stability window.

Frank L.: posted short update to customers: "Mitigation applied, success rate improving; follow-up with root cause and timeline forthcoming."

incident-bot: thread closed for active paging but remains for post-incident tasks.
